messages.author: 3a915c3a91d0b053
messages.subject: LBA extensions thread
parts:
Hi,

I'm making a separate thread for extensions to the LBA model. Since I'm doing a lot of fiddling with the model, I thought it would be productive to share the code. Unfortunately, running the models takes very long on my current equipment, so I am unable to test all of these (I am testing only those that are relevant to my current project). All the extensions are made for the group-level LBA estimation (choiceRT_lba.R), and NOT for the individual one (choiceRT_lba_single.R) I will do my best to update this thread.

TESTED means I tested parameter recovery of the model. UNTESTED means I either run the individual model without testing recovery accuracy, or just wrote the code without running it (in that case the code might contain some unexpected syntax errors).

Please feel free to incorporate these to the package or use these individually (but be sure to first test parameter recovery of the untested models).

1. Allowing different parameters to vary per condition.
 To run these STAN files one needs to adjust 'modelPath' in the R function 'choiceRT_lba.R'

 - separate T0 (non-decision times) per condition (DONE, TESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_t.stan
 - separate A (starting-point variability) per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_A.stan
 - separate d (boudary - A) per condition  (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_d.stan
 - separate A & d per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_Ad.stan
 - separate A & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_At.stan
 - separate d & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_dt.stan
 - separate A, d  & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_Adt.stan

2. Fixing Decision Boundary (A+d) instead of drift-rate variability (s)
To run these in addition to 'modelPath' one needs to adjust the estimated parameters as well in the R function

 -  IN PREPARATION

3. Adding trial-based model regressors
- IN PREPARATION

4. Adjusting the choiceRT_lba.R function to accommodate all the models
- when everything else is ready


Additionally, things I'll maybe add given enough time:

5. Adding individual regressors (i.e. some individual difference measures)

6. R function (or a set of functions) to generate posterior predictive estimates (simulated data given individual model parameters using rtdists package)
This might not be needed, as this functionality is already implemented, but I honestly don't know whether it works correctly, as I get very weird estimated when trying to use it (refer to the forum thread about posterior predictive in LBA).


Best,
Wojciech

messages.author: 3a915c3a91d0b053
messages.subject: Re: LBA extensions thread
parts:
Hi,

Judging by the error, I believe the issue might be that you need to used a modified R function to run the model. The original function choiceRT_lba.R has built in model path associated with stan function (line 120). You need to adjust this by giving the path associated with your stan function. 

Additionally, you should remove all instances of  allIndPairs variable from the R function, as it will most likely produce an error, and the information there is redundant, so there is no loss in doing so. 

One temporary convenient way of modifying the R function I found, is to use trace(choiceRT_lba, edit=T) function call in R. It enables you to temporarily modify the choiceRT_lba function (untill reloading the library).

Hope this helps,

Best,
Wojciech
